name: polyarthritis overview
title: Polyarthritis (four or more joints): the joint fluid sorts it into non-inflammatory (osteoarthritis), inflammatory (crystals; seropositive rheumatoid arthritis; the seronegative spondyloarthropathies psoriatic, axial and reactive; and the connective tissue diseases lupus, dermatomyositis and scleroderma) or infectious; each disease has photos of its extra-articular signs, a mnemonic and its targeted tests

root.title: FOUR or more joints: what does the JOINT FLUID say, and what PATTERN?
lines: aspirate a red, hot joint: infection or crystals? · normal fluid is clear, white cells under 200
every inflammatory arthritis is a CLINICAL diagnosis: history, extra-articular clues, then targeted tests

groups.title: INFLAMMATORY: synovitis = swelling, warmth, pain, stiffness
lines: fluid: cloudy yellow · white cells > 2000 · neutrophils > 50% · crystals possible

tiers.title: CRYSTAL
lines: onset in hours to days · episodic

tiers.title: SERONEGATIVE spondyloarthropathy
lines: rheumatoid factor negative · asymmetric or axial · erodes

tiers.title: CONNECTIVE TISSUE DISEASE: antinuclear antibody (ANA)
lines: negative ANA rules it OUT · positive rules nothing in · then the specific antibody

head: h
Osteoarthritis
DEGENERATIVE · insidious, rises with age

pics.caption: Heberden's and Bouchard's nodes
pics.credit: lecture slide, © American College of Rheumatology

pics.caption: X-ray: DIP and thumb-base narrowing, spurs

clue: • DIPs, PIPs, thumb base, big toe
mn: B before H, base to tip
Bouchard's at the PIP (nearer the body), Heberden's at the DIP (the tip)
inv: osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis and cysts, ASYMMETRIC narrowing

head: h
Gout and pseudogout
crystals: acute, red, comes and goes

pics.caption: Tophi on the ear
pics.credit: lecture slide, © American College of Rheumatology

pics.caption: Podagra: the big toe
pics.credit: lecture slide, © American College of Rheumatology

clue: Gout: small joints of the foot · pseudogout: knee
mn: gout: Negatively birefringent Needles (yellow) · pseudogout: Positive rhomboids (blue)
inv: gout: needles, negative · pseudogout: rhomboid, positive
pseudogout: look for hemochromatosis, hyperparathyroidism, hypothyroidism

head: h
Rheumatoid arthritis
warm, swollen, not red

pics.caption: Rheumatoid nodules
pics.credit: lecture slide, © American College of Rheumatology

pics.caption: Ulnar deviation, MCP subluxation
pics.credit: lecture slide, © American College of Rheumatology

clue: Wrists, knuckles, finger joints, ankles, feet
mn: knuckles and middle finger joints, never the DIPs; OA and psoriatic take the tips
inv: Rheumatoid factor + anti-CCP: only if suspected
• positive = more aggressive · NEVER to monitor

head: h
Psoriatic arthritis
also asymmetric: gout, reactive

pics.caption: Skin psoriasis
pics.credit: lecture slide, © American College of Rheumatology

pics.caption: Nail pitting
pics.credit: lecture slide, © American College of Rheumatology

mn: Plaques · Pitted nails · Puffy (sausage) digits · Painful heel (enthesitis)

head: h
Axial spondyloarthropathy
e.g. ankylosing spondylitis
clue: psoriasis · inflammatory bowel disease · recent infection
mn: Psoriatic · Ankylosing spondylitis · Inflammatory bowel disease · Reactive

head: h
Reactive arthritis
triggered by an infection

pics.caption: Vesicopustular skin lesion
pics.credit: lecture slide, © American College of Rheumatology

mn: Can't see, can't pee, can't climb a tree

head: h
Systemic lupus erythematosus
also symmetric, like RA

pics.caption: Malar rash
pics.credit: lecture slide, © American College of Rheumatology

pics.caption: Discoid lupus
pics.credit: lecture slide, © American College of Rheumatology

mn: Serositis · Oral ulcers · Arthritis · Photosensitivity · Blood · Renal · ANA · Immunologic · Neurologic · Malar · Discoid
inv: flare: anti-dsDNA ↑, complement C3 and C4 ↓

head: h
Dermatomyositis
inflammatory myositis with skin signs
clue: • shawl, V and holster signs · mechanic's hands
mn: heliotrope on the eyelids · Gottron's over the knuckles · shawl, V and holster sit where clothes do

head: h
Scleroderma
systemic sclerosis

pics.caption: Sclerodactyly
pics.credit: lecture slide, © American College of Rheumatology

pics.caption: Raynaud's phenomenon
pics.credit: lecture slide, © American College of Rheumatology

mn: Calcinosis · Raynaud's · Esophageal dysmotility · Sclerodactyly · Telangiectasia
inv: ANA, then anti-centromere, anti-Scl70, anti-RNA polymerase 3

head: h
Infectious arthritis
bacterial · viral · early gonococcal
pic: redness only with infection or crystals
clue: • viral: during or weeks after the infection
hepatitis A, B, C · HIV · CMV · EBV · parvovirus · chikungunya · influenza · COVID-19
mn: Red and hot: put a needle in it
over 75% neutrophils + bugs on Gram stain = septic
inv: self-limited · supportive; NSAIDs or a short prednisone course if severe

panels.title: Synovial fluid: aspirate to decide
items: normal: clear · thick · white cells < 200 · neutrophils < 25%
inflammatory: yellow, cloudy · moderate · > 2000 · > 50% · crystals possible
infectious: yellow-green, cloudy · thin · > 2000 · > 75% · Gram stain and culture POSITIVE

panels.title: Acute (6 weeks or less) or chronic?
items: acute: infectious and post-infectious (incl. viral) · crystals · rheumatic fever · drug reaction (serum sickness) · EARLY autoimmune
chronic: rheumatoid · connective tissue disease · seronegative · palindromic · vasculitis · polyarticular JIA · Still's · sarcoidosis
many acute forms become chronic if autoimmune

panels.title: Tests for everyone (safety + inflammation)
items: blood count: anemia of chronic disease, platelets ↑ (inflammation), low counts (autoimmune)
creatinine and liver enzymes (drug clearance) · C-reactive protein (sedimentation rate not routine)
don't order ANA and RF reflexively: think of the differential first

panels.title: X-ray: who erodes?
items: erodes: rheumatoid, psoriatic and other spondyloarthritis, gout, septic
little help when acute: damage takes years
